subject: c-act
title: C.ACT.------DYM.F.
description: Diagram in CMBA-29, the first on book p273. (C)C-ACT (composite activism) is crossed with DYM-F (dynamic functionalism). The diagram is densely populated with prefixed nodes — (R)INDIV-TD (the reality of individual tendencies), (R)LANG (the reality of language), (P)RE-DIF (the point of activation of redefinitions) — flagging Braxton's specific interest in distinguishing the *real* and the *point-of-activation* layers from concept-level operations. C-ACT outputs to DYM-F (the crossing) and MT-INFO (music information) → INFO-F (information focus). A parallel chain: TR (transformation) → C-CONT (composite continuance) → ALT-F (alternative functionalism). ALT-F branches to GRAD (gradualism) → (R)INDIV-TD → (R)LANG and (R)INDIV-TD → (P)RE-DIF; ALT-F also outputs to SOC-RT-P (social reality particulars). Structural argument: composite activism crossed with dynamic functionalism produces music-information → information-focus as one chain, and transformation → composite-continuance → alternative-functionalism as a parallel chain. Alternative functionalism's outputs are politically loaded: gradualism producing the reality of individual tendencies — the very mechanism Braxton names as the western device for absorbing change — which then produces the reality of language and only conditionally (point-of-activation prefix) reaches redefinitions. Social reality particulars is a sibling output. The diagram thus diagrams how composite activism's productive line passes through *exactly* the gradualism-mechanism that the section's prose identifies as the institutional capture device.
